verdict.rationale: ComplyAdvantage Mesh has a documented API that an agent could drive. It supports creating and screening customers synchronously or asynchronously, receiving WORKFLOW_COMPLETED webhooks with screening results, looking up customers by external identifier, and setting per-customer monitoring for ongoing re-checks. Its API credentials have configurable permissions and an optional expiry. However, it is an AML screening pipeline rather than identity-document verification, and no MCP surface is documented. Missing for 10: identity-verification sessions with extracted document data, an explicit polling/outcome endpoint or on-demand re-check trigger, an MCP server, and hands-on corroboration of agent-driven operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the verification pipeline — create sessions, poll outcomes, retrieve extracted data, and trigger re-checks through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: These can be generated in the ComplyAdvantage Mesh web application under Settings > Access Management > API Credentials, where you can also configure their permissions and optional expiry date.
Synchronous screening: Ideal for real-time onboarding workflows where low latency is critical. Asynchronous screening: Suitable for high-volume screening scenarios
Set up a webhook of type `WORKFLOW_COMPLETED`... Refer to the `customer-screening.step_output.screening_result` field in the webhook payload to determine if any hits were found
This endpoint allows you to set the monitoring configuration for a single customer.
Cases, alerts and risks can be reviewed and remediated either via the ComplyAdvantage Mesh web application or by integrating with the API for use in your own case management system.
